subject: food-technology
source_note: Topic structure follows the CCEA A-Level Nutrition & Food Science specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: A2 2 — Research Project

connections.why: Protein needs are expressed through Dietary Reference Values used to evaluate diets
Carbohydrate is the body's main energy source feeding into energy balance
Saturated fat and blood cholesterol are key modifiable risk factors for cardiovascular disease
Blood-sugar effects and glycaemic load link carbohydrate intake to type 2 diabetes
Antioxidant vitamins are part of the dietary influences on cancer risk
Sodium intake is a recognised modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease
Nutritional needs through life are quantified using DRVs and EARs
A sustained positive energy balance leads to overweight and obesity
Obesity is a contributory factor in the development of cardiovascular disease
Excess body fat is a major risk factor for type 2 diabetes
Physical activity raises energy expenditure, helping maintain energy balance
Alcohol is a lifestyle influence linked to increased cancer risk
Changing eating patterns drive the rising prevalence of diet-related disorders
Comparing intakes against requirements reveals trends in the population's diet
Food security challenges are addressed through more sustainable food systems
Reducing food waste is a central part of food sustainability
Tackling food poverty depends on changing consumer purchasing behaviour
Food safety is delivered through shared responsibility along the food chain
Controls along the food chain aim to minimise microbiological contamination
Microbiological risks are regulated through EFSA and the EC food hygiene package
Allergen information is governed by food labelling and safety legislation
Diet-related disorders motivate the sustainable consumer choices studied in Option A
Modern food consumption and supply patterns raise the safety concerns of Option B
Diet-related disorders provide rich synoptic topics for the research project
Nutritional analysis methods underpin the primary research planned in the project
